claims.text: Controlled thermal pre-oxidation can form a thin, continuous, adherent Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A pre-formed Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale will improve the alloy's high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The protective scale is stable and slow-growing under extreme-temperature service.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys normally form non-protective, porous, or volatile oxide scales during high-temperature oxidation.
Heating at approximately 1000°C for one hour under controlled oxygen partial pressure will form the proposed protective scale.
A continuous, dense chromium- or aluminum-oxide scale limits oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
The engineered oxide layer retards rapid oxygen uptake by acting as a diffusion barrier.
The engineered oxide layer prevents formation of non-protective, spalling oxide scales.
After 100 hours at approximately 1100°C in air or pure oxygen, pre-oxidized samples will have significantly lower oxidation mass gain than untreated samples.
After the service exposure, pre-oxidized samples will retain a more uniform and adherent oxide scale than untreated samples.
Lower mass gain and a more adherent scale will enhance structural integrity under extreme-temperature service.
An untreated refractory high-entropy alloy exposed at 1100°C in an oxygen-rich environment for 100 hours develops rapidly growing, non-protective oxides, high mass gain, and degradation.
The benefit is limited to alloy compositions on which pre-oxidation can produce a uniform, adherent Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on alloy composition, oxide identity, and pre-oxidation parameters.
The hypothesis is falsified if pre-oxidized samples show neither a statistically significant reduction in mass gain nor a continuous, adherent protective scale relative to untreated controls.
